summary: Victoria Song reviews Amazon's third-gen Echo Frames, testing the Carrera Cruiser model for a week. They look more stylish and have better battery life and somewhat improved bass, but they work mostly as open-ear headphones with Alexa, which isn't compelling on the go. At up to $389.99 they're pricey compared with Ray-Ban Meta Smart Glasses and Bose Frames, so Amazon is closer on form than on function.
one_line: Victoria Song's review finds third-gen Amazon Echo Frames (Carrera Cruiser) stylish with better battery but weak bass, audio leakage, mediocre Alexa and high price.
key_facts: The Carrera Cruiser model of the third-gen Amazon Echo Frames costs $389.99; the Verge Score is 6 and it was listed at $314.99 at Amazon.
Third-gen Echo Frames start at $269.99 for clear lenses, $299.99 for blue light filtering, and $329.99 for sunglasses.
Lens options are clear, prescription, blue light filtering, and sunglass, in round, cat eye, square, rectangle, and "modern" rectangle shapes.
Amazon continues its Carrera partnership; the Cruiser and Sprinter both cost $389.99, and the Cruiser only comes with sunglass lenses.
The Cruiser is made of lightweight acetate weighing 46.3g but felt plasticky, and slipped down the reviewer's low nose bridge.
Bass is purportedly three times better, but it is still weaker than standard AirPods, and audio leaks noticeably in quiet spaces like an office.
Battery gave about five hours of media playback and calls with about 30 percent left; a roughly 50-minute call drained about 20 percent, and a full charge takes about 2.5 hours.
The charging stand requires placing the glasses vertically with lenses pointing up, and the reviewer preferred the charging case of Meta's smart glasses.
Alexa can now make non-Alexa calls and, on Android, reply to texts, but directions were clunky and once suggested Bowling Green, Kentucky instead of a nearby Manhattan train station.
The Echo Frames can pair with multiple devices and switch between them, which Ray-Ban Meta Smart Glasses weren't really capable of.
A VIP Filter limits notifications to select apps and contacts, and the glasses only play a sound rather than read texts aloud.
Ray-Ban Meta Smart Glasses start at $299, only $30 more than the cheapest Echo Frames, with better build, camera, audio, mic and transition lens options.
Bose Frames Tempo and Soprano retail for $249, can be found for around $200, and have similar battery life and better sound quality.
